 Telangana Will Telangana schools get Saturdays off? MLC proposes five-day week
 Subhransu Satpathy 8 Nov 2026 7:46 AM Share this: HYDERABAD: Teacher MLC Malka Komaraiah has urged the Telangana government to introduce a five-day working week for schools and make changes to the government holiday calendar, citing students’ welfare and the cultural significance of festivals.
 In a representation to Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, Komaraiah proposed Monday-to-Friday classes, with Saturdays declared holidays. He cited the anticipated impact of El Niño, rising temperatures and growing water concerns. 
 He said the temporary arrangement would help conserve water and energy, reduce traffic and pollution, and protect students’ health and well-being.

 To maintain academic continuity, he proposed extending school hours by 35 to 40 minutes from Monday to Friday.
 In a separate representation dated November 7, 2026, addressed to the secretary of the Education Department, the MLC sought changes to the government’s 2026 holiday calendar. 
 He requested that the government declare November 9 (Monday) a general holiday for Deepavali instead of November 8 (Sunday). He pointed out that the festival holiday coincided with the weekly holiday.
 According to the representation, the Amavasya tithi begins on Sunday and continues until Monday. He said a separate holiday on Monday would allow government employees, teachers and their families to celebrate the festival.
 I have submitted a representation to the Secretary, Education Department, Government of Telangana, requesting suitable modifications to the Government Holiday Calendar 2026, including declaring November 9 (Monday) as a General Holiday in place of November 8 for Deepavali.
 I have also requested General Holidays for Raksha Bandhan and Varalakshmi Vratham, and the inclusion of Tholi Ekadashi and Ratha Saptami in the Optional Holidays list, considering their cultural, religious and traditional significance. I urge the state government to consider these requests favourably in the interest of government employees, teachers and their families.
 @revanth_anumula @TelanganaCMO @TelanganaCS
 — MALKA KOMARAIAH (@MalkaKomaraiah) November 7, 2026 
 MLC seeks recognition for four important festivals
 Komaraiah also proposed changes to the holiday calendar to recognise the state’s cultural and religious traditions.
 He sought a general holiday for Raksha Bandhan, citing its cultural and traditional significance. He also requested a general holiday for Varalakshmi Vratham, particularly considering its religious importance and observance among women.
 He proposed including Tholi Ekadashi and Ratha Saptami in the list of optional holidays.
 The MLC requested the government to consider the proposals and take appropriate action, keeping the cultural, religious and traditional sentiments of people, particularly government employees and teachers, in view.
 He sought an early and favourable decision on the representations.
